findings.title: Pillar Two noncurrent income taxes payable ($9.82B) is not addressed in the net cash or FCF rationale
findings.detail: Not repaired: the candidate is unchanged since review 1 (valuation_inputs.json sha256 f228676b... and note.md cdf16378... match generator/manifest.json, and computed/ equals numerical/recompute/). I re-checked this in a fresh context. The 10-K says 'Other noncurrent liabilities included $9.82 billion and $648 million related to income taxes payable as of September 3, 2026 and August 28, 2025, respectively' (periodic.txt line 3101). MD&A ties the increase to Pillar Two: 'higher noncurrent income taxes payable related to the implementation of Pillar Two' (line 1832). The $9.03B FY2026 Singapore top-up tax is at line 3099. History shows FY2026Q4 CFO of $43.973B, which carries most of the deferral. FY2026 FCF excluding the roughly $9.6B other-noncurrent-liabilities inflow would be about 37% of revenue rather than 44.3% (my arithmetic). The fcf_margin rationale says Q4 CFO was 'flattered' by this item and that 'A recurring Pillar Two tax deferral is possible upside but is not assumed'. But neither fcf_margin nor net_cash says how the $9.82B balance already accrued is treated. That cash sits in reported cash, so it is inside net cash of $68.274B. It is not deducted, and its payment is not in the FCF path. Size, my own arithmetic and not code output: $9.82B / 1,145M diluted shares is about $8.6 per share on both legs. The blended value would be about $1,093, upside about +5.6%, and the rating stays Neutral. This is a judgment of the same kind as the customer deposits (asm-002), so it should be stated. Minor.
findings.required_evidence: The valuation_inputs.json net_cash or fcf_margin rationale states how the $9.82B noncurrent income taxes payable is treated: deducted as debt-like, paid inside the FCF path, or a rolling operating liability with no adjustment. It gives the reason and an approximate per-share sensitivity labelled as analyst arithmetic.

findings.title: The rating depends on the DCF/EV-Sales weight, and the note does not show the relative-value leg
findings.detail: Not repaired: the candidate is unchanged since review 1. I re-verified the figures. Code output (numerical/recompute/valuation.json): DCF $862.83 per share and relative EV/Sales $1,818.58 per share (15.121x x $133.188B + $68.274B, over 1,145M shares). At dcf_weight 0.75 the blend is $1,101.77, TP $1,102, +6.39%, Neutral. My own arithmetic, not code output: Outperform needs TP >= $1,191.22, which holds at a DCF weight of about 0.656 or less. Underperform needs TP <= $932.26, which holds at a weight of about 0.927 or more. The note (note_rendered.md, Model and valuation section) still shows only the DCF per-share value and the peer multiple. It does not show the relative-value leg, the 75/25 weights, or that the rating rests on the weighting. Constraint on the repair: values.json (38 keys) has no key for relative_per_share or dcf_weight, so under the untagged-number gate the writer cannot show those numbers until the code owner adds the keys. A qualitative sentence, labelled our view, saying the two methods diverge widely and the rating is sensitive to the weighting needs no new key and can be added now. Minor; the inputs are inside policy and the dcf_weight rationale exists.
findings.required_evidence: note.md adds one sentence, labelled analyst judgment, saying the relative-value method gives a much higher per-share value than the DCF and that the Neutral rating depends on the 75/25 weighting. If code keys for relative_per_share and dcf_weight become available, the note shows them through {{key}}.

checked: Candidate identity: generator file sha256 values match generator/manifest.json (assumptions 6fd8b7f5..., valuation_inputs f228676b..., note cdf16378..., mapping 53268da0..., narrative b0a82e15...). All five computed/*.json files are byte-identical to numerical/recompute/. gates.json has no findings. The candidate is unchanged since review 1.

Open findings in my area: asm-004 and asm-005 are not repaired, so both are reported again under the same IDs, minor. prov-005 belongs to provenance. The same 'returned only if' wording also appears in the valuation_inputs net_cash rationale, but it does not change any figure, so I left it to prov-005.

Next-quarter revenue vs guidance: FY2027Q1 forecast is $61.501B, at the guided midpoint of $61.5B +/- $1.5B (Q-1). That is +13.41% on the 14-week FY2026Q4 base of $54.229B, or about +22% on a 13-week base. The 53-week year (Q-10) is explained in the rationale.

Next-quarter margins vs guidance: GM 85.95% equals the GAAP guidance (Q-2). Opex is $2.312B against the GAAP guidance of $2.31B (Q-3). Tax is 14.8%, the FY2026 ETR (periodic.txt line 1737, Pillar Two). EPS of $37.50 is inside $37.84 +/- $1.00 (Q-4), and the shortfall is explained by excluded interest income.

Later-quarter path: revenue +8%/+5%/+3% q/q to $71.8B in FY2027Q4, decelerating from FY2026 (+20.6%, +74.9%, +73.7%, +30.8%). GM flat on supply limits and price-band floors (Q-8, Q-9). Opex held at 3.76% of revenue, against a pre-Q4 run rate of about $1.7B (FY2026Q3 R&D $1.316B + SG&A $0.407B) and $2.77B in the 14-week Q4. Plausible and explained.

Valuation inputs: WACC 10.5% (cyclical premium, analyst judgment, inside [6%, 16%]). Terminal growth 3.0% (inside [0%, 4%] and below WACC). Terminal value is 55.9% of EV, below the 80% flag. Recomputed TV = $61.695B x 1.03 / 0.075 = $847.28B, PV $514.30B.

FCF margins vs history: FY2025 4.5%. FY2026 44.3% (CFO $89.675B - capex $30.712B on $133.188B, from eu.py history quarterly sums), or about 37% excluding the Pillar Two noncurrent tax deferral (see asm-004). Years 1-5 are 50/50/42/35/30%. Year 1 is reconciled to the guided capex (periodic.txt line 1771) and to working capital. Terminal 30% is below the FY2025-26 pooled 35.5%.
Revenue growth years 2-5 (+5%, -10%, -15%, -5%): cycle-normalisation judgment with a rationale. Year-5 revenue is $205.7B, against FY2026's $133.2B, supported by price-band floors (Q-9).

Net cash completeness against the balance sheet (periodic.txt about lines 2017-2052): cash 38,364M, short-term investments 5,070M, long-term marketable investments 30,019M, current debt 491M, long-term debt 4,688M. Net cash is 68,274M, which matches valuation.json. Customer contract liabilities of 12,895M are excluded with a reason and a sensitivity (asm-002, resolved in review 1). Noncurrent income taxes payable of 9.82B within other noncurrent liabilities of 11,659M are not addressed (asm-004). Unearned government incentives of 786M are operating and need no adjustment. Non-marketable equity investments of about 1.30B are excluded with a reason.

Peer set: INTC, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC (IDM and WFE companies on the memory capex cycle). There is no memory peer, and the caveat is stated in the note and the rationale. Peer TTM ends 2026-06-27 to 2026-07-26 (CY2026Q2), against MU FY2026Q4 ending 2026-09-03 (CY2026Q3). The alignment is noted.
Arithmetic spot-checks: relative leg (15.1215 x 133.188B + 68.274B) / 1.145B = $1,818.58. Blend 0.75 x 862.83 + 0.25 x 1,818.58 = $1,101.77, TP $1,102, upside +6.39%, Neutral under the policy bands.

Share count: the valuation uses 1,145M (latest tagged diluted count, FY2026Q3), against 1,147M in the release for Q4 and a +0.3% per quarter forecast drift. The effect on value per share is about 0.2-1%, immaterial, and the data gap is disclosed in the note.

Rationales exist for every assumption and valuation input and support the numbers chosen. The gaps in the net cash and FCF judgment and in the visibility of the weighting are recorded as asm-004 and asm-005.
